title: TTHM and HAA5 MCL compliance calculation: locational running annual average (LRAA) under subpart V, running annual average (RAA) under subpart L, and increased monitoring

conditions: Subpart V applies to community and nontransient noncommunity water systems that use a primary or residual disinfectant other than ultraviolet light, or deliver water treated with one (141.620(b))
exclusions: Transient noncommunity water systems are not subject to subpart V (141.620(b))

claims.subject: Locational running annual average (LRAA)
claims.value: The average of sample analytical results for samples taken at a particular monitoring location during the previous four calendar quarters
conditions: The same definition is recorded on page dbp.definitions (claim.dbp.definitions.lraa-computation); this page carries the compliance mechanics built on it
Subpart V applies to community and nontransient noncommunity water systems that use a primary or residual disinfectant other than ultraviolet light, or deliver water treated with one (141.620(b))
exclusions: Transient noncommunity water systems are not subject to subpart V (141.620(b))

claims.subject: How TTHM and HAA5 MCL compliance is calculated under subpart V: the LRAA at each monitoring location
claims.value: Each LRAA, calculated at each monitoring location from subpart V monitoring results, must not exceed the MCL; the subpart V MCLs are compliance with maximum contaminant levels based on locational running annual averages

conditions: Subpart V applies to community and nontransient noncommunity water systems that use a primary or residual disinfectant other than ultraviolet light, or deliver water treated with one (141.620(b))
exclusions: Transient noncommunity water systems are not subject to subpart V (141.620(b))

claims.subject: How TTHM and HAA5 MCL compliance was calculated under subpart L (system-wide RAA) compared with subpart V (LRAA per location)
claims.value: Under subpart L, for systems monitoring quarterly, compliance was a running annual arithmetic average, computed quarterly, of quarterly arithmetic averages of all samples collected by the system, with no per-location test; under subpart V each monitoring location's LRAA is tested against the MCL
conditions: This claim states the two averaging bases as the sources define them; it asserts no reason for the change and no comparison of outcomes
Subpart V applies to community and nontransient noncommunity water systems that use a primary or residual disinfectant other than ultraviolet light, or deliver water treated with one (141.620(b))
exclusions: Transient noncommunity water systems are not subject to subpart V (141.620(b))

claims.subject: TTHM and HAA5 LRAA computation by systems monitoring quarterly
claims.value: Calculate the LRAA from subpart V monitoring results and determine that each LRAA does not exceed the MCL; more than one sample in a quarter at a location is averaged into one quarterly value; if four consecutive quarters are not completed, compliance is based on the average of the available data from the most recent four quarters

conditions: Subpart V applies to community and nontransient noncommunity water systems that use a primary or residual disinfectant other than ultraviolet light, or deliver water treated with one (141.620(b))

claims.subject: TTHM and HAA5 LRAA determination by systems monitoring annually or less frequently
claims.value: Each sample must be less than the MCL; a sample that exceeds the MCL brings the increased-monitoring requirements of 141.625; when no sample exceeds the MCL, each location's sample result is its LRAA
conditions: 141.620(d)(2) says each sample must be less than the MCL and names 141.625 for a sample that exceeds it; 141.625(a) states the trigger as a TTHM sample >0.080 mg/L or a HAA5 sample >0.060 mg/L, so under 141.625(a) a sample exactly equal to the MCL does not trigger increased monitoring; whether such a sample meets 141.620(d)(2) is not stated by either quote and is not classified by this page

claims.value: Quarterly monitors: at the end of the fourth calendar quarter following the compliance date and at the end of each subsequent quarter, or earlier if an LRAA from fewer than four quarters would exceed the MCL regardless of later results; less-than-quarterly monitors: beginning with the first compliance sample taken after the compliance date

claims.subject: When subpart V monitoring begins
claims.value: Quarterly monitors begin in the first full calendar quarter that includes the compliance date; less-than-quarterly monitors begin in the calendar month recommended in the IDSE report under 141.601 or 141.602 or identified in the subpart V monitoring plan under 141.622, no later than 12 months after the compliance date

claims.subject: Subpart V compliance dates by system size
claims.value: Systems serving 100,000 or more: April 1, 2012; 50,000 to 99,999: October 1, 2012; 10,000 to 49,999: October 1, 2013; fewer than 10,000: October 1, 2013, or October 1, 2014 if Cryptosporidium monitoring is required under 141.701(a)(4) or (a)(6); consecutive and wholesale systems in a combined distribution system: the earliest compliance date in that combined distribution system
conditions: The dates apply to systems that are not part of a combined distribution system and to the system serving the largest population in one; the State may grant up to 24 additional months for compliance with MCLs and operational evaluation levels where capital improvements are required
